narrative.overview:
SplitWise AI is the precise little tool you take out at the table, settle the bill with and put away. Every screen answers one money question: who paid, who owes, and how much is left. The interface stays calm and exact so the numbers can carry each screen. One blue does the work of the brand. Slate neutrals hold the structure. Other colours appear only when they carry meaning: a budget's status, or which way money is flowing between people.

Density is compact but not cramped. Body copy is 14px, cards are white on a pale slate page, and there is one clear primary action per view. The system is quick and confident: the next thing to do always has the strongest contrast on the screen, feedback comes straight away, and nothing decorative gets in the way of a number. It is built for a 390px phone first and opens out into two to four columns on larger screens.

This look rejects three things. Fintech flash: no gradients, glass, neon or glow. Emoji used as UI. And any second brand hue.
keyCharacteristics: A single Ledger Blue accent; any other colour is semantic: status or money direction.
System sans type, with numbers in semibold and tabular figures.
Flat white cards with a hairline border and a barely visible lift.
Gently rounded corners: 8px for controls, 12px for cards, 16px for sheets.
Mobile first. Modals become bottom sheets on phones.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Ledger Blue is the only brand hue. If a new element wants a colour and isn't an action, a status or a direction of money, it stays slate.

rules.name: The Two Semantics Rule
rules.body: Budget status (green / amber / red) and money direction (green / orange) are separate vocabularies. Owing money is not an error, so balances never use the critical red.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: A status colour always comes with an icon (✓, !, ✕) and a text label ("On track", "Close to limit", "Over budget"). Money direction always comes with words ("gets back", "owes").

rules.name: The Numbers Lead Rule
rules.body: In a row, the amount is the heaviest text. Names are 500, amounts 600, and surrounding words regular.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Any amount that sits in a column or might be compared uses tabular-nums. Amounts are always formatted by formatINR, never by hand.

rules.name: The Float-Only-When-Floating Rule
rules.body: Only overlays get more than the card-rest shadow. Hover never lifts a card. Hover changes the fill colour instead.

dos: Do use Ledger Blue for actions and the active state only. Charts use Series Blue.
Do pair every status colour with its icon and label, and every balance colour with "owes" or "gets back".
Do show amounts with formatINR in semibold with tabular-nums wherever they sit in a column.
Do start every grid at grid-cols-1, and check it at 390px with no horizontal scroll.
Do keep one filled primary button per view. Everything else is secondary or ghost.
Do use a white card with a hairline border, 12px corners, 20px padding and shadow-sm for any new content block.
donts: Don't use emoji as UI: no 👋 in greetings, 🎉 in empty states or ✨ on the AI insights heading. Use words, or an SVG icon if one is really needed.
Don't add a second brand hue (purple for AI, teal for groups and so on). AI surfaces use Ledger Blue Wash.
Don't use gradients, glassmorphism, neon or glow effects. Every fill is a solid colour.
Don't colour a debt in critical red. Owing money is Owes Orange, not an error.
Don't lift cards on hover or give them shadows heavier than shadow-sm. Only overlays float.
Don't use dual axes or several series hues in a chart. Magnitude is shown in Series Blue only.
